newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO say Hebron deal with Israel not likely soon.
newsitem.headline: PLO say Hebron deal with Israel not likely soon.

text.p: Palestinian officials on Friday accused the United States of bias and said a deal with Israel on the handover of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian control was not likely soon.

"Most of the essential points we have not resolved," a senior Palestinian official, who did not want to be identified, told Reuters. When asked if a deal on Hebron was far off, the official responded: "Yes."
Both Israeli and Palestinian negotiators have said recently that a U.S.-brokered deal on the long-delayed transfer of 80 percent of the volatile city to Palestinian rule was near.

Israeli officials have blamed the Palestinians for delaying a deal. "There is a desire on behalf of the Palestinians to stall and to delay and to drag it on," said David Bar-Illan, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's media adviser.

But Palestinian Minister Nabil Shaath said PLO negotiators were now "facing a big problem with the Israeli side". He said Israel refused to commit to target dates for further pullbacks after Hebron, as stipulated in previous peace deals.

"I think all that is happening shows that the American position is not neutral but in many situations the Americans take a position very close to the Israeli position, which makes reaching an agreement difficult," Shaath said after the weekly cabinet meeting in Gaza on Friday.
"Sometimes the American co-sponsor implies that we are creating new issues as if we are delaying the negotiations, as if there is a desire not to reach the liberation of Hebron," he said.
In Washington, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns rejected suggestions that the Palestinians were to blame for the failure this week to conclude the Hebron accord.
Some 400 Jews live among more than 100,000 Palestinians in Hebron, a flashpoint of violence. Israel was to have redeployed its troops in Hebron some 10 months ago under a 1995 interim agreement.
